children: The Consumer Price Index report for August indicated a 3.4% year-over-year increase to match the consensus expectation.

Airfares in the U.S. rose 23.4% in August compared to a year ago on an unadjusted basis, according to data compiled by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics. By comparison, airfares were up 25.5% in July, 36.5% in June, and 26.7% in May. Airfares were up 2.7% sequentially, compared to the level in July, and have risen in seven of the last eight months. Overall, core inflation was up 2.5% year-over-year during the month.

Airfares have jumped this year mainly because jet fuel prices spiked due to the Iran conflict, sharply increasing operating costs across the airline industry. A lower level of hedging has impacted the ability of airlines to offset the higher jet fuel costs. Analysts forecast U.S. jet-fuel prices are likely to remain elevated and volatile through the rest of 2026, with the central expectation being a gradual easing only if Middle East oil flows and refinery output normalizes.

title: CPI read: Airfares rise 23% in August as the hot streak continues
